docs.title: Learn by building.
docs.lead: Practical guides to take an idea from its first repository to a review that is ready to merge. Use the web interface, the terminal, or both.
docs.startHereBody: Create an account, open your workspace, and create a repository. In a few minutes, you can save changes and ask AI to explain the diff.
docs.quickstartBody: AIVerse organizes your work into repositories. Each repository contains files, branches, and commit history. The sidebar shows the current state, and the history keeps confirmed changes.
docs.quickstart1: Create an account and choose a username.
docs.quickstart2: Open your workspace and create a repository with a short name.
docs.quickstart3: Add or edit files in your local environment and check the status.
docs.quickstart4: Stage your changes, write a clear message, and create a commit.
docs.quickstart5: Ask the assistant to explain a change, find risks, or suggest a message.
docs.repositoriesBody: A repository is a project's workspace. Choose a descriptive name, explain what it does, and set visibility to match its contents.
docs.publicBody: may appear in Explore so other people can discover it.
docs.privateBody: for work you do not want to show publicly; always check who has access.
docs.descriptionBody: summarizes the purpose, status, and how to run the project.
docs.commitsBody: group related changes and explain the intent, not just the modified file.
docs.secretsWarning: Before publishing, look for API keys, passwords, `.env` files, tokens, and personal data. If a secret reaches a commit, revoke it; deleting it from the latest version does not remove earlier copies from history.
docs.terminalBody: The CLI can initialize repositories, stage files, save commits, inspect history, and sync with an AIVerse server.
docs.cloneIntro: To clone a project hosted on the server:
docs.terminalTips: Use `add` to select files for your next commit. Check the status before committing. Keep messages brief, imperative, and focused on the outcome.
docs.aiIntro: AI is a learning and review tool. Give it a specific task, and stay in control of which suggestions you adopt.
docs.reviewChangesBody: share the diff and ask about risks, edge cases, and useful tests.
docs.explainCodeBody: ask what a function does, including its inputs, effects, and dependencies.
docs.learnBody: ask for small examples and an explanation tied to the files you have open.
docs.commitsImproveBody: ask for a title that describes intent and scope.
docs.conflictsBody: ask it to compare both changes, explain the impact, and suggest options.
docs.promptTips: A good prompt includes the goal, relevant context, and the response format you want. For example: “Review this diff for authorization flaws. Name the file, the abuse scenario, and the smallest fix. Do not rewrite the whole module.”
docs.protectBody: Requests to external providers may send diff text to the provider configured by the operator. Never include credentials, secrets, or personal data.
docs.reviewsIntro: A useful review shares context and makes a decision easier. Open a pull request with its goal, scope, design choices, and verification steps.
docs.reviews2: List the main changes and sensitive areas.
docs.reviews3: Explain how to test it and what to expect.
docs.reviews4: Ask specific questions and respond to each thread.
docs.reviews5: Before merging, check tests, security, accessibility, and documentation.
docs.reviewsClosing: AI can help set priorities, but the reviewer decides whether a change is ready.
docs.privacy1: Use a unique password and a password manager.
docs.privacy2: Do not publish customer data, credentials, or information you are not allowed to share.
docs.privacy3: Grant only the access needed and revoke it when it is no longer useful.
docs.privacy4: Check repository visibility before posting or asking for public help.
docs.privacy5: If you expose a key, revoke it immediately and review the provider's usage logs.
docs.privacy6: Understand what content is sent to AI before requesting a review.
docs.backendFix: Check that the service is running, the API's HTTPS URL is set in `VITE_API_URL`, and the web domain is allowed by `WEB_ORIGIN`.
docs.sessionProblem: Your session won't stay signed in
docs.sessionFix: Check HTTPS, secure cookies, CORS credentials, and that the configured origin exactly matches the website domain.
docs.aiFix: The operator must configure a provider key and allow network requests. Features that rely on an external model will be unavailable without it.
docs.postFix: Sign in, check your connection, and make sure the content is within the character limit. Publishing requires a database connection.
docs.updated: This guide describes the current beta and will be updated as the product changes.
legal.title: Legal notice
legal.serviceIntro: AIVerse is a web platform for code version control, collaboration, and AI assistance. This site describes a beta and may change during development.
legal.pendingBody: The repository does not identify AIVerse's legal owner or provide an address or contact channel. The operator must add these details before offering the service to the public.
legal.owner: Owner or legal entity: not provided.
legal.address: Country and contact address: not provided.
legal.email: Support and privacy email: not provided.
legal.ipBody: AIVerse's name, marks, and interface identify this service. Users retain rights to the code they contribute and must be authorized to share it. Read our
legal.availabilityBody: The platform is in beta and provided as available. It may contain bugs, be interrupted, or change. Third-party links and services are governed by their providers' terms.
legal.draft: This notice is an informational draft. It does not replace the operator's legal identification or applicable legal review.
legal.cookiesIntro: AIVerse uses necessary technical storage to maintain sessions and protect account actions. This app does not use advertising cookies or analytics tools.
legal.sessionCookie: keeps you signed in. It is an HttpOnly cookie so JavaScript cannot read the session identifier; in production it is marked Secure.
legal.csrfCookie: helps verify that actions submitted from the interface are legitimate. It does not contain the session; in production it is sent over HTTPS.
legal.browserPrefsBody: Your theme and language are saved in browser local storage, not in cookies. You can clear them in your browser's privacy settings; AIVerse will then return to its defaults.
legal.controlBody: If you block necessary cookies, you may be unable to sign in or perform protected actions. This version does not load optional advertising or measurement cookies.
legal.cookiesBetaBody: This notice reflects the reviewed application code. The operator should update it if analytics, advertising, embedded videos, or other browser storage services are added.
legal.privacyIntro: This policy explains what data AIVerse processes and how it is used. The legal operator and privacy request channel still need to be published; see the
legal.accountData: Account data: username, display name, email address, and password stored as a secure hash.
legal.usageData: Usage data: sessions, saved browser preferences, repository metadata, activity, and pull requests.
legal.codeData: Code: versioned content is stored in persistent backend storage; metadata is stored in MongoDB.
legal.technicalData: Basic technical data, such as IP address, error logs, and security activity, may be processed on Render, Vercel, and MongoDB Atlas infrastructure.
legal.aiReviewsBody: When you request an AI review, the diff or text you submit is sent from the backend to the provider configured by the operator (Google Gemini in the current setup). Do not include passwords, tokens, private keys, or personal data in your code. The provider's own terms and policies apply to its processing.
legal.cookiesPrefsBody: We use necessary cookies to maintain sessions and protect actions from unauthorized requests. Your selected theme and language are saved locally in your browser. No advertising cookies or analytics tools are configured; see the
legal.visibilityBody: Public repositories may appear in Explore. Keep private any content you do not want to share. We retain data while the account or repository remains active; account deletion is not yet available in the interface during this beta.
legal.requestsBody: You may request access, correction, or deletion of information. A contact channel is not configured in this release and must be published before the service is offered to the public. Do not share private data in public issues.
legal.thirdPartiesBody: The app may rely on Render for the backend and persistent storage, Vercel to serve the interface, MongoDB Atlas for the database, and Google Gemini for AI when enabled. Each provider may process technical data needed to provide its service.
legal.termsIntro: These terms cover use of AIVerse, a version control and collaboration platform currently in beta. By creating an account or using the service, you agree to follow these rules.
legal.yourAccountBody: Provide a valid email, protect your credentials, and tell us if you suspect someone accessed your account. You are responsible for activity under your session.
legal.yourCodeBody: You retain rights to the code you upload. You authorize us to store, process, and display it to operate AIVerse according to your visibility choice. Public repositories may appear in Explore; do not upload information you have no right to share.
legal.acceptableUseBody: Do not use AIVerse to distribute malware, compromise systems, abuse other users, infringe third-party rights, or disrupt the service. We may limit or suspend accounts that pose a risk to the platform or community.
legal.billingStart: Current plans and prices are shown under
legal.billingBody: . If the operator enables checkout, subscriptions are billed monthly in COP through Mercado Pago. Before subscribing, check the displayed price and the payment provider's terms.
legal.betaAvailabilityBody: The platform changes often, and some features may fail, change, or become unavailable. We do not promise continuous availability or an error-free service. Keep independent copies of important work.
legal.terminationBody: You may stop using the service at any time. The interface does not yet let you delete your account or cancel a subscription. The operator should publish a support channel for these requests.
legal.changesBody: These terms may change as the product evolves. The update date will appear at the top of this page. The operator details and contact channel have not yet been published.
legal.betaClosing: These texts describe current features and need legal review and the operator's contact details before a public launch.
